 SFC Environmental Technologies is an environmental technology firm offering efficient technologies and comprehensive engineering solutions for wastewater treatment (“WWT”), wastewater recycling & reuse (“WRR”), and solid waste treatment (“SWT”). 
The IPO will be open for subscription on October 27, 2026, and close on October 29, 2026. SFC Environmental Technologies is a Mainboard IPO with a price band set between ₹313 to ₹330 per share. As per the RHP, the company plans to raise around ₹668 crores through an Initial Public Offering (IPO).

 SFC Environmental started its business in 2005 by providing design, technology, manufacturing, supply, and supervision for installation and commissioning of equipment for the treatment of wastewater. The company uses its own wastewater treatment C-Tech technology for treating sewage and effluents. 
 For medium- to long-term investment, this IPO might be a good fit. Overall, investors should carefully evaluate the company’s fundamentals, strengths, risks, and growth prospects before deciding whether to invest. 
 Strengths: 
 SFC Environmental was the first technology provider to introduce C-Tech technology in the SBR space, an advanced wastewater treatment technology. 
 The company has established itself as a well-positioned market leader in the municipal solid waste management sector by offering a wide range of waste management solutions, including OREX and GWMC technologies.
 The firm has maintained a strong, long-standing relationship with customers, which leads to repeat business and a strong order book of ₹1,656.64 crore as of August 31, 2026. 
 Its revenue from operations grew at a CAGR of 10.56%, from ₹657.50 crore in FY24 to ₹803.63 crore in FY26. PAT increased at a CAGR of 5.42%, from ₹144.17 crore to ₹160.21 crore. PAT margins stood at 19.94% in FY26.
 Weaknesses:   
 Its revenue and business depend on its C-Tech technology. Failure to upgrade or innovate these technologies or fail to develop new ones can adversely impact its results of operations. 
 The firm derives about 84.98% of its revenue from the WWT and SWT segments, and it is dependent on projects, contracts, or works awarded or funded by government entities. If they fail to win projects, or any reduction or termination in such projects can negatively affect its business and financial condition. 
 SFC Environmental earns a major part of its revenue from the top 10 customers, and they do not hold long-term contracts with them. Loss of any of the top customers can badly impact the overall business and financial condition.
 Its business operations require high working capital to meet its working capital needs. Failure to secure sufficient funding could adversely affect its operations, cash flows and financial condition.
